propositions: When two bundle objects exist for a single ref in S3, git-remote-s3's cmd_push rejects pushes before writing anything and clone fails with 'multiple updates for ref not allowed', making the store unclonable.

Upstream's git-s3 doctor is interactive-only (blocks on input() at EOF) and discards non-chosen heads by side-branching to orphan refs, causing permanent loss of events unique to discarded heads in an append-only event log.
The heal must merge all divergent bundle heads losslessly via iterated 2-parent git merges (not octopus or merge=union), following sync's existing _union_merge semantics, with no events discarded.

The heal acquires the helper's S3 per-ref lock, re-enumerates bundles under the lock (TOCTOU guard), fetches all heads locally, merges them into a single new bundle, writes that bundle before deleting any originals, then cleans up—ensuring at least one lossless bundle survives every crash point.

Concurrent repair processes race safely: exactly one acquires the helper's per-ref lock and performs the merge; others receive None/412 and back off, converging on the winner's collapsed remote on their next push retry.

The heal runs under rebar's write_lock to serialize against local committers, with the helper's S3 lock as the outer lock and rebar's write_lock as the inner lock, forming a cycle-free order that prevents local/remote mutations from interleaving.
